title: Before you grow, define what the business should give you
angle: Distinguish a personal destination from a growth route; define trade-offs and a review date.

title: The price of a successful deal
angle: Work through a hypothetical growth offer whose obligations conflict with the owner's desired role.

title: Delegation without decision rights is another reporting layer
angle: Define authority boundaries and a bounded delegation test; do not cite unverified statistics.

title: Before agreeing on growth, agree on what it is for
angle: Separate individual priorities, common business commitments and decisions that require consent.

title: Build an alternative before you need it
angle: How a feasible second route changes a decision without becoming a threat or bluff.

title: Measure the result you actually wanted
angle: A hypothetical owner seeking reduced operating involvement needs metrics beyond revenue.

title: When your greatest strength becomes the company's dependency
angle: Convert personal relationships into reliable organizational capability without dismissing their value.

title: What would make you change your mind?
angle: Make disconfirming evidence explicit before a strategic commitment; distinguish uncertainty from failure.

title: Decide which decisions you need to keep
angle: Control is not necessarily involvement in every routine action; write reserved decisions explicitly.

title: A good offer can still be the wrong next move
angle: Compare an offer with the stated destination rather than the appearance of momentum.

title: Do not build a strategy on what you assume a partner wants
angle: Separate stated interests, documented rights and unverified assumptions in negotiations.

title: A strategy needs a review date, not an expiry excuse
angle: Set an explicit review and distinguish a useful adaptation from endless drift.
